newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: GRAFOBAL SALES RISE 58 PCT IN H1 1997.
newsitem.headline: GRAFOBAL SALES RISE 58 PCT IN H1 1997.

text.p: Paper packaging producer Grafobal said on Thursday that its sales during the first-half of the year rose to 13.47 million litas from 8.53 million litas in the same period in 1996.
Director general of the company Stanislovas Jurkuvenas told Reuters that the increase in sales was due to growing exports.
The company exported around 40 percent of its products in the first half of the year, 80 percent of it to Belarus and the rest to Russia and Latvia.
"June was very successful for the company and we forecast our net profit for the first six month of the year to be no less than 500,000 litas," Jurkuvenas said.
He said the exact profit figures will be known on June 19.
The company had 270,000 losses in the first half of 1996 and reported a tiny 15,000 litas net profit for the whole year.
Grafobal said earlier its net profit for the first five months of the year was 320,000 litas.
Grafobal is a 78-percent Slovak owned firm and is listed on the A group of Vilnius bourse.
